ledger_conventions.pl_rounding: Each play settles to a 2-decimal P/L (American-odds payout rounded at settlement). Running units = sum of these rounded per-play values, so the ledger column sums EXACTLY to the total (sportsbook-settlement convention, chosen for auditability). Note: summing unrounded payouts can differ by ~0.01u (e.g. baseline 7/23 is +0.48u rounded, +0.49u unrounded).
ledger_conventions.brier_ab: raw-vs-shrunk Brier/logloss compared only on plays where BOTH probabilities exist (engine skips produce no shrunk_p). 7/23 n_both=4 (Dobnak excluded).
ledger_conventions.objective: profitability = EV vs price break-even, NOT win% > 50%.

decision_policy_version.definition: The whole decision path a play passes through: projector + selector thresholds + intake guards + settlement maths. A change to ANY of them starts a new version, because the plays the new path produces are not exchangeable with the plays the old one produced.

components.projector: engine.kprops proj(): START-ONLY accumulation; K-rate prior 0.22 at 80 TBF; E[TBF] prior 24.0 at 3 starts; returns nothing below 5 GS
components.selector: engine.kprops select_play(): EV>0; edge>=0.04 against the conditional-on-settling probability p/(1-p_push); |proj-line|>=0.8; side==sign(disp); weight 0.5 if GS<10
components.intake_guards: short-line hold: any arm posted at <=3.5 K is rejected without --allow-short-lines (added 2026-07-27, lineage b23c254)
components.settlement: probs(ek,line) -> (p_over, p_push, p_under); ev() three-outcome (added 2026-07-27, commit 91d2d9c)

experiment_queue.title: Opponent-K% adjustment for K-props
experiment_queue.method: log5/odds-ratio combine of pitcher as-of shrunk K-rate p with as-of opponent team K-rate-taken o [o = (SigmaSO + L*N0)/(Sigma(AB+BB) + N0), N0=200, denominator AB+BB per principal 7/24] vs league L: adj=(p*o/L)/((p*o/L)+((1-p)(1-o)/(1-L))); E[TBF] unchanged; Poisson tails unchanged. experiment_queue.title: Is V13's disagreement with the moneyline market an edge or a favorite-fading bias?
experiment_queue.motivation: Across 50 priced+uncapped game-rows on 5 cards, mean(V13_home_wp - market_home_wp) is -0.086 where the home team is a big favorite (mkt>0.58, n=8), -0.019 in the middle (n=40), +0.005 where home is a big dog (n=2). V13 compresses toward 50/50 relative to the market. Every ml_ev_tracking pick so far (KC +154, COL +186, STL -116, COL +265, NYY +140) is consistent with that shape: 4 of 5 are underdogs. The ledger may be one systematic bet — 'fade favorites' — wearing five different uniforms.
experiment_queue.hypothesis: H0: V13's favorite-fade is genuine edge -> ml_ev_tracking picks show positive CLV. H1: it is calibration bias -> CLV is <=0 and units bleed even when W-L looks respectable.
experiment_queue.primary_readout: Closing-line value in cents, NOT win-loss. Pre-specified because W-L is the wrong readout for a +EV objective function.
experiment_queue.holdout: Forward slates from 2026-07-27 onward. The 7/25 and 7/26 rows are EXPLORATORY — they generated this hypothesis, so they cannot confirm it.
experiment_queue.blocking: Requires a genuine closing snapshot at lock, which has never yet been captured. E4 cannot start until closing capture works. This is the same binding constraint (price access) already logged.
experiment_queue.must_not_do: This diagnostic MUST NOT be used to veto or trim picks on 7/26 or any registered slate. Rule 4 forbids discretion; the whole point of pre-registration is that a mid-flight hunch does not get to edit the pick list.

known_issues.text: p_over returned P(X>=ceil(line)), scoring an integer-line push as an OVER win. probs() now returns (p_over,p_push,p_under) and ev() settles three outcomes. Proven no-op on the record -- all nine graded rows are half-point lines. Independently re-verified 2026-07-27: back-compat bit-for-bit across 240x12 half-point cases, push mass matches closed-form Poisson, and the -110 EV flip +6.81% -> -9.14% reproduces.
known_issues.exposure_scope: Measured, not asserted. Across the K-PROP population only - all 10 board files under data/mlb/props/ - there are 365 posted line values and ZERO are integer; every distinct value is a half-point (1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5, 5.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5, 9.5, 11.5, 12.5). So no K prop captured to date could have hit the bug, and the fix is preventive for this market. This does NOT extend to the board population as a whole: stored GAME-TOTAL boards contain 25 integer lines (7.0/8.0/9.0/10.0/11.0), which push exactly the same way. Totals are safe today only because daily_card.py:102 emits a directional lean rather than a price. An earlier statement of this scope said '0 of the 4 line values in any captured board' - wrong twice: the scan keyed on a "line" field and so missed the positional [book, line, under, over] format that holds essentially the whole population, and 'any captured board' wrongly swept in the totals boards. Corrected 2026-07-27.

known_issues.text: The engine's single largest claimed edge on the first real price board (Fedde OVER 2.5 @ +106, EV +0.469) sits on the lowest line on the board. A 2.5 K line IS the market telling us it expects a short outing. The engine's E[TBF] prior does not read that signal, so it projects a full start and manufactures an edge. Freeland (1.5), Avila (1.5) and Baz (2.5 at DK) have the same shape. Treat a posted line at or below 3.5 as evidence about TBF, not as value.

Residual (E[K] - posted line) correlates with the posted line at -0.87 on the 7/26 board. Direction of every selection is nearly determined by whether the line is high or low. Until E5 settles this, no K selection should be read as genuine information.

The board looks like 30 priced arms and is not. 8 of 30 rows carry no price at all, the Hard Rock column is cut off entirely, and only 12 arms have any two-sided quote. Total usable two-sided quotes: 31.

Rung coherence passed on 100% of rows including ones that are plainly alt-line ladders (Misiorowski 12.5). T2 can no longer be cited alone as evidence that a board is a real per-book market. T3 dispersion is the load-bearing test.

This board arrived after first pitch for 26 of 30 arms. The engine's first-ever look at a full real price board is therefore a shadow measurement, not a slate. A board captured pre-lock remains the single highest-value missing input.

engine_vs_market_shrinkage.design: OLS of the engine's pre-slate E[K] on the board's median posted line. Slope 1.0 = the engine moves with the market. Slope < 1.0 = the engine is over-shrunk toward the mean and will mechanically buy every low line and sell every high line.

clean_and_gs_ge_15.implied_stretch_ESTIMATOR: 1.42 is 1/slope, the noiseless inversion. It is the right answer only if the posted line is treated as error-free truth and the goal is to restore dispersion. For finding edges it is the wrong one: restoring dispersion amplifies the engine's own noise along with any signal, and noise in excess of the market's is precisely what manufactures edges.

engine_vs_market_shrinkage.finding: The engine's point projections are under-dispersed relative to both outcomes and the market. DIRECTION is consistent across every cut and both yardsticks. MAGNITUDE is not identified. The four comparable point estimates span 1.08-1.35; this is not a confidence interval or an identified parameter range, and no-stretch remains plausible. The outcome-side evidence is not significant on its own (SE 0.515, 95% CI [0.28, 2.42], t vs no-stretch 0.68). The previously stated 'about 1.42x' was the noiseless inversion, the most aggressive of the three estimators.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.why_the_filter_matters: Unfiltered the slope reads 0.426 (stretch 2.35x). The quarantined alt-rung rows alone would have inflated the required correction by roughly 65%. Measuring on dirty rows would have produced a much more aggressive and wrong engine change.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.convergence: This is the SECOND independent measurement pointing the same way. The 7/25 out-of-sample grade gave an OLS slope of actual-on-projected of 1.35 (n=24, outcome-based). This board gives an implied stretch of 1.42 (n=12, market-based). Outcomes and prices are independent yardsticks and they agree on both the direction and roughly the magnitude.
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.status: HYPOTHESIS-GENERATING ONLY. Neither measurement was pre-registered, both are n<=24, the two never converged, and no engine change is licensed by either (R7).
engine_vs_market_shrinkage.RETRACTED_2026_07_27_convergence: RETRACTED. Original text: "This is the SECOND independent measurement pointing the same way. The 7/25 out-of-sample grade gave an OLS slope of actual-on-projected of 1.35 (n=24, outcome-based). This board gives an implied stretch of 1.42 (n=12, market-based). Outcomes and prices are independent yardsticks and they agree on both the direction and roughly the magnitude." The two numbers are different estimands, so the agreement was an artifact of pairing one estimator with another. 1.35 is a calibration slope, actual regressed on projected. 1.42 is a noiseless inversion, 1/slope(E[K]~line). Since slope(y~x)*slope(x~y) = corr^2, inverting one never yields the other. Proof: apply the market document's own estimator to the outcome data and it returns 1/slope(proj~actual) = 1/0.1760 = 5.68, not 1.35. Kept verbatim per R6. Credit: Taco.

estimators_computed_consistently.source: outcome side recomputed from the 24 stored rows in data/mlb/box/2026-07-25_grades.json; market side derived from the slope/corr already stored in this object
estimators_computed_consistently.dispersion_matching_LABEL_NOTE: Row renamed 2026-07-27. It previously read 'sd-matching, Poisson noise stripped', which was wrong for half the row: only the OUTCOME estimate is Poisson-stripped. The outcome figure removes Poisson sampling variance from actual K counts, sqrt(var(actual) - E[lambda]) / sd(proj). The MARKET figure is sd(line)/sd(E[K]) = corr/slope with no Poisson correction of any kind - posted lines are not Poisson draws and there is nothing to strip. Labelling both cells the same way implied a symmetry that does not exist. Credit: Taco.
estimators_computed_consistently.the_pair_that_was_quoted: 1.35 from row 1 and 1.42 from row 3 -- one estimator from each row.
estimators_computed_consistently.correction_to_the_first_correction: The 7/27 retraction in docs/core_breakdown.html put the outcome-side sd-matching figure at 1.56. That was computed from an ASSUMED mean of 4.9. The 24 stored rows give mean(actual)=5.750 and sd(actual)=2.723, so the Poisson-stripped talent sd is sqrt(7.413-5.750)=1.290 and the ratio to sd(proj)=0.983 is 1.31, not 1.56. An assumed input inside a correction is the same R1 error the correction was fixing. SUPERSEDED WORDING (kept per R6): 'The honest range narrows from ~1.1-1.6 to ~1.1-1.35.' That phrasing reads as an interval estimate and it is not one. The four comparable point estimates span 1.08-1.35; this is not a confidence interval or an identified parameter range, and no-stretch remains plausible.
estimators_computed_consistently.caveat: The Poisson strip assumes K counts are conditionally Poisson. Real counts are mildly over-dispersed (variable IP), which inflates the stripped talent variance, so 1.31 is an upper bound on that estimator. At n=24 it is in any case very noisy.
estimators_computed_consistently.comparable_estimates_span: The four comparable point estimates span 1.08-1.35; this is not a confidence interval or an identified parameter range, and no-stretch remains plausible.
estimators_computed_consistently.what_comparable_means: The 2x2 of calibration slope and dispersion matching: 1.35 / 1.08 / 1.31 / 1.24. The noiseless-inversion row is excluded because it is not comparable across sources - 5.68 against 1.42 - which is the arithmetic that made the original 'convergence' claim possible in the first place.
